- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) mid-horizon, model underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–3 days) — add 1–3% to forecast for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse — add 2–4% upward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns positive.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags — forecast should rise 1–3 days after sentiment change, not immediately.
